description: Search arXiv papers by query with category and sort filters. Returns paper metadata including title, authors, abstract, categories, and links.

category.description: Restrict results to an arXiv category. A leaf code ("cs.CL", "math.AG") matches exactly. A bare archive code ("astro-ph", "cond-mat", "cs", "math") matches the whole archive — its subject classes plus the legacy flat papers filed before the archive was subdivided. Note "physics" is the general-physics archive (physics.*), not the wider physics group: astro-ph, cond-mat, hep-*, quant-ph and the rest are separate archive codes. Use arxiv_list_categories to discover subject classes.

max_results.description: Maximum results to return. Default 10. At most 50 are returned per call: a larger value returns the first 50, and when more matches exist the response says how to reach them — the start of the next page, or date windows once paging cannot reach them all. arXiv serves only the first 10000 results of a query, so a page reaching past result 10000 can come back cut short at it, and the response says so. Each result includes title, authors, abstract, and metadata — keep low to limit response size.

query.description: Search query. Field prefixes: ti: (title), au: (author — search the surname and narrow a common one with a category or topic: au:hinton AND cat:cs.LG; a quoted name such as au:"geoffrey hinton" matches when one author's name holds every quoted word, in any order, and an initial does not match a spelled-out first name), abs: (abstract), cat: (category — a leaf code matches exactly, a bare archive code such as cat:astro-ph matches its whole subtree), co: (comment), jr: (journal ref), all: (all fields). Boolean operators, uppercase only: AND, OR, ANDNOT. Space-separated terms are joined with OR, so "quantum computing" matches papers with either word; AND requires every term ("quantum AND computing"). The operators share one precedence and group to the right ("a AND b OR c" reads as "a AND (b OR c)"), so use parentheses for any other grouping. Quote a multi-word topic to match it as a phrase, and put alternatives in parentheses before a filter so the filter applies to all of them: '"graph neural networks" AND cat:cs.LG', '(ti:transformer OR ti:attention) AND cat:cs.CL'. arXiv ignores common words such as of, the, and, for, in, so leave them out or keep them inside a quoted phrase. Examples: "au:bengio AND ti:attention", "all:transformer AND cat:cs.CL".

sort_by.description: Sort criterion. Use "submitted" for newest papers, "relevance" for best query matches.

sort_order.description: Sort direction. "descending" returns newest/most relevant first.

start.description: Pagination offset (0-10000). Use with max_results to page through results. E.g., start=10 with max_results=10 returns results 11-20. arXiv serves only the first 10000 results of a query, so a page reaching past result 10000 can come back cut short at it and a start of 10000 can be refused. To reach later matches, carve the search into submitted_from/submitted_to windows and page within each.

submitted_from.description: Earliest submission date to include, inclusive, as a UTC YYYY-MM-DD date. Omit for no lower bound.

submitted_to.description: Latest submission date to include, inclusive, as a UTC YYYY-MM-DD date. Omit for no upper bound. Both bounds are inclusive, so consecutive windows ("2024-01-01".."2024-01-15" then "2024-01-16".."2024-01-31") cover the matches with no gap; a paper submitted at exactly the midnight seam between two windows appears in both, so de-duplicate collected results by paper id. That is the way to reach matches past the start ceiling: split the date range, then page within each window.

name: arxiv_search_papers

cap.description: The page size applied: max_results, or 50 when max_results asks for more — fewer when the page was cut short at result 10000, the last one arXiv serves.

effectiveQuery.description: The query as actually searched, carrying every filter applied — the category subtree and submitted-date window folded into arXiv syntax alongside the supplied terms. Replaying it as `query` with no other filters reproduces this exact result set.

error.description: Present when the call failed. Absent on success.

code.description: JSON-RPC error code for this failure.

reason.description: Machine-readable failure mode. Declared by this tool: `unknown_category`: Provided category code is not part of the arXiv taxonomy. `rate_limited`: arXiv has throttled requests (HTTP 429 or "Rate exceeded." body). `invalid_request`: arXiv rejected the request (HTTP 4xx other than 429), typically malformed query syntax. `unsupported_query_syntax`: The mirror search engine rejected the FTS5 expression the query translated to. Every query the translator accepts is meant to parse, so this marks a translator defect. `invalid_date_range`: submitted_from or submitted_to is not a real UTC calendar date, or the window starts after it ends. `start_beyond_result_limit`: start is 10000 or more on a search arXiv answers, past the first 10000 results it serves for any query. Other values are possible when a failure originates below the handler.

recovery.description: Actionable next step for the caller.

message.description: Human-readable description of what went wrong.

notice.description: Recovery guidance when results are empty or paging overshot. Absent on successful pages.

pageStart.description: Pagination offset of this result page.

items.description: arXiv paper metadata — identifier, title, authors, abstract, categories, and links.

categories.description: All arXiv categories assigned to this paper.

totalFound.description: Total matching papers before pagination. Exact, except for a search the local mirror answers with no free-text term that spans several category codes (a whole archive such as cat:cs, or two categories) or filters by submitted date alone: the mirror stops counting such a search at 50,000, and a total of 50,000 there carries totalFoundIsLowerBound and means 50,000 or more.

totalFoundIsLowerBound.description: Present when totalFound is a floor: at least that many papers match. Absent when totalFound is exact.

truncated.description: True when more matching papers exist beyond this page (totalFound > start + shown).

title: Arxiv Search Papers
